newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wearnes expects second half to match.
newsitem.headline: Wearnes expects second half to match.

text.p: Wearnes Ltd, a subsidiary of WBL Corp, said on Tuesday it expects the operating result for its second half to match lower first half profits.

For the six months ended March 31 1997, the company, which has interests ranging from distribution of automobiles to telecommunications, reported a 28 percent fall in net profit to Singapore $8.02 million.
It said in a statement accompanying the half-year results that profit margins for mobile phones would continue to be under pressure, but telecom infrastructure and technical services should improve.

The company also said its recent proposal to sell its 51 percent interest in O'Connor's Corp Bhd and to buy 49 percent in O'Connor's Properties Sdn Bhd should result in an extraordinary gain of about $55.45 million.

The transaction should boost group net tangible assets by 30.3 cents to S$1.099 per shares but will not have any material impact on group earnings for the financial year ending September 30 1997, the statement said.
